inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted average used for diluted EPS in the CY2025 annual report (2,152,830,513; basic 2,129,696,013 plus ~23m vested/unvested performance rights). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows at 0.2% of revenue, so diluting the count as well would double-charge. Buybacks are zero in every year of the history.
inputs.sbc_source: CY2025 annual report (RSG.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:7494) share-based payments expense US$1.8m; no equity-award tax withholding disclosed (kpis EquityAwardTaxes = 0 every year). Interest income of US$6.6m NOT stripped because the company is in net DEBT at the anchor date once the Doropo deferred consideration is counted (rule applies only when net cash is material).
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in USD (reporting currency switched AUD->USD at the CY2018/CY2019 boundary); ASX quote in AUD. All per-share values computed in USD then converted at USD/AUD 1.4249 (Yahoo AUDUSD=X 0.7018, 2026-09-25T04:36Z). No liquid dual listing remains for a parity check (the LSE line was withdrawn); the company's own AUD-cent dividend history is the only cross-reference. refresh_price.py moves the price but never this rate.
inputs.net_debt_note: Dec-2025 balance sheet (RSG.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:6460-6475, 3148-3163). Cash 62.6 + fixed-term deposits 68.1 = 130.7. Total debt 201.5 = bank overdraft 46.2 + borrowings 11.7 (3.5 current + 8.2 non-current, truck financing) + Doropo deferred consideration 136.7 at carrying value (75.2 current: US$50m due Nov-2026 plus US$25m Guinea-permit in-lieu; 61.5 non-current: US$75m due Nov-2027) + lease liabilities 6.9. Bullion on hand (31,242 oz, US$134.6m at Dec-25 spot) is EXCLUDED from cash because it was sold in H1-2026 and sits inside the Y1 revenue projection (H1-26 sold 123,951 oz against 104,795 oz produced). Cross-check: company-defined net cash (cash + deposits + bullion - overdraft/borrowings, before the Doropo consideration) was US$209.1m at Dec-25 and US$317.4m at 30-Jun-26; the H1-26 interim is not yet extracted so the Jun-26 balance sheet cannot be used as the anchor without double-counting H1-26 flows that are already inside Y1. Ravenswood promissory notes (A$68m vendor note + up to A$150m upside note) and the ~US$31m Loncor sale proceeds are excluded from the bridge as uncertain/one-off; both are upside to the bridge, not downside.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built rate: 10-yr UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.15 = ~10% cost of equity for a mid-cap gold producer, plus ~1pp for single-region West African (Mali/Senegal/Cote d'Ivoire) jurisdiction risk = 11%. Debt is immaterial (net-debt-to-EBITDA ~0.2x) so WACC ~ cost of equity. The SAME 11% is used in all three scenarios; gold-price cyclicality, the Mali fiscal regime and Doropo execution are carried in the scenario flows and weights, not in per-scenario discount rates (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A) leases as debt: lease liabilities (US$6.9m at Dec-25) sit in total_debt; lease principal (US$3.8m/yr) is NOT deducted from the flows. Immaterial either way (<0.5% of revenue).
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows: the Governments of Mali (20% of Syama/SOMISY, 10% of SOMIFI), Senegal (10% of Mako/Petowal) and Cote d'Ivoire (10% free-carried Doropo) take their profit share after tax. Modelled as a combined cash-tax-plus-leakage driver (base 42% = ~33% cash income tax on EBIT + ~14% of post-tax profit to NCI; CY2025 actuals: tax 85.2/234.6 = 36% book, 58.9 cash; NCI 20.6/149.4 = 13.8%). The US$45.3m NCI balance-sheet stock is therefore NOT deducted in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF with MID-CYCLE commodity treatment (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md; no memory entry, first valuation). Resolute is a single-commodity gold producer: Syama (Mali, ~70% of output), Mako (Senegal, stockpile processing only, ~55-65koz/yr until ~2027), Doropo (Cote d'Ivoire, US$516m build, first gold H1-2028, ~170-200koz/yr). Revenue is modelled as ounces x realised price; the price path is the mid-cycle judgement: CY2026 at ~US$4,300-4,700 (H1-26 already realised US$4,712/oz; spot US$4,305 on 2026-09-25, 52-wk 3,764-5,586), gliding to US$3,000/oz by 2030 in the base case (the price Resolute itself uses for the Doropo DFS NPV; reserves are priced at US$1,950). Running 10 years at spot would not be a valuation, it would be a gold call. CY2026 is Y1: H1-26 actuals (revenue 584.7, 123,951 oz sold) plus H2 on the 21-Sep-2026 cut guidance (group 205-225koz, AISC US$2,250-2,350/oz). EBITDA margins are built from AISC: CY2025 company EBITDA 397.7 (46%) less indirect taxes 36.8, obsolete consumables 9 and other 6 = ~40% on a US$3,125/oz realised price; at US$3,000 with Doropo's US$1,406/oz LOM AISC blended in, the mature margin is ~43%. Horizon 10 years because production and capex are not steady until Doropo is fully ramped (~2030). Cap multiples are cyclical-miner low (bear 10x / base 12x / bull 14x). Currency: USD flows, AUD quote (see fx_note). Currency-switch history: pre-CY2019 rows are AUD and are not used in any CAGR. The Mali settlement (US$159.9m, 2024) is a sunk one-off; its lasting effect is the 2023 Mining Code (~US$250/oz added to Syama's cost base per the Analysis JSON), which IS in the margin paths. Working-capital capture -3% of revenue change (stores/consumables and receivables grow with the Doropo ramp). SBC-light (0.2% of revenue): house and street bases nearly coincide; band_position is close to degenerate and should be read as such.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 10-year revenue CAGR (CY2025 865.6 -> Y10 ~1,325): Doropo/SSCP volume growth net of the mid-cycle gold-price glide. Historical CAGRs are not usable as a forward proxy for a price-taker whose production fell 395koz (CY2020) -> 277koz (CY2025) while revenue rose on gold.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR -2.9% vs revenue 5yr +7.5% (divergence >30%): revenue growth is gold price, not volume; book value was cut by the CY2021 US$227m impairment and the CY2024 Mali settlement/loss. EPS 5yr CAGR (+30%) compounds from a near-zero CY2020 base and the owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (+61%) from a CY2022 trough; neither is meaningful.
historical_growth.notes: All CAGRs on the USD series only (CY2020->CY2025 for 5yr, CY2022->CY2025 for 3yr); CY2016-CY2018 are AUD and excluded. Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC (no interest-income strip, net debt positive): CY2020 -42.2, CY2021 -6.8, CY2022 22.7, CY2023 34.2, CY2024 9.1, CY2025 94.6. The 5yr owner-FCF CAGR is null because the CY2020 base is negative. Owner-FCF CAGR (n/a) below reported-FCF CAGR (n/a) is not the finding here; SBC is ~0.2% of revenue and immaterial.

base.growth_note: Ounces x realised US$/oz. Y1 CY2026: H1 actual 584.7 + H2 ~110koz x ~$4,300 = ~1,058 (+22%). Y2 2027: Syama recovers to ~200koz with SSCP + Mako 55koz stockpiles = 255koz x $3,700 = ~944. Y3 2028: Doropo first gold H1, ~100koz partial year + Syama 210 + Mako 30 = 340koz x $3,400. Y4 2029: 450koz x $3,200. Y5 2030: 460koz x $3,000 (mid-cycle). Y6-Y10: price +2%/yr nominal, volume drifting 450 -> 400koz as Doropo falls from its 204koz first-five-year average toward its 170koz LOM average and Mako's stockpiles end without a life extension.
base.margin_note: Y1 48%: H1-26 company EBITDA 55.4% at $4,712 realised, H2 ~40% at ~$4,300 with Syama AISC $2,300-2,400 and indirect taxes (~4% of revenue) deducted. Y2+ 43%: at $3,000-3,700 gold, blended AISC ~$1,750 (Syama ~$2,000, Doropo $1,406 DFS, Mako ~$1,800) less ~$250/oz sustaining capex = cash cost ~$1,500, plus indirect tax ~$120/oz and corporate+exploration ~$85/oz at 450koz. Royalties fall mechanically with price (~$20/oz per $100). Drifts to 42% in Y8-10 as Doropo grades decline.
base.capex_note: Y1 CY2026 guided US$310-360m total (Doropo 170-190). Y2 2027: Doropo balance ~US$300m of the US$516m build + sustaining ~100 + SSCP tail = ~US$420m (44% of a trough-price revenue year). Y3 2028: Doropo tail + sustaining = ~US$160m. Y4+: sustaining ~$250/oz x 450koz + ~US$40-50m/yr life-extension and exploration = 11-12% of revenue; D&A converges to 12% (D&A ~ capex at steady state, so the model does not perpetuate a tax shield).
base.tax_note: 42% combined cash tax + NCI leakage, flat: Mali 2023 Mining Code (30% CIT plus state profit share) on ~70% of output, Senegal 25-30%, Cote d'Ivoire 25% + 10% free carry from 2028. CY2025 actual: 36% book tax and 13.8% NCI share of post-tax profit = ~45% combined on book, ~40% on cash. No Doropo tax-holiday credit assumed.

bull.growth_note: Gold holds a higher plateau: CY2026 H2 at $4,500 (Y1 ~1,103), then $4,300 / $4,100 / $3,900 / $3,600 flat-real thereafter, still BELOW today's spot of $4,305 in every year from 2028. Volumes: Syama back to 200koz+ in 2027 and 210-250 with Syama North; Doropo on time and at its 204koz first-five-year average; Mako life extension (Tomboronkoto) keeps ~50koz; group reaches the 500koz target in 2029 and holds it. Y7+ +2.5%/yr is price inflation on flat volume.
bull.margin_note: 50%: at $3,600-4,300 with the same cost base as the base case, EBITDA/oz ~$2,000-2,300 after royalties, indirect tax and overheads. Cap 14x, still a miner's multiple.
bull.tax_note: 40%: Cote d'Ivoire's lower fiscal take on a larger Doropo share of profit.

bear.growth_note: Gold mean-reverts and Mali stays hard: CY2026 H2 at $4,000 with only ~105koz (Y1 ~1,005, H1 is banked); 2027 235koz at $3,200 as Syama's A21 pit ramps slowly; 2028 Syama-only 200koz at $2,600 (the CY2024 average) with Mako's stockpiles exhausted and no life extension; Doropo slips a year to 2029 (80koz) and 2030 (180koz) with the build overrunning to ~US$650m; Y7-10 -2%/yr on Syama grade decline.
bear.margin_note: At $2,600 Syama's cash cost (~$1,850 post-Mining-Code plus overheads) leaves ~20%; Doropo lifts the blend to 30%. Y2-Y3 owner FCF is deeply negative (build capex on trough revenue) and is funded from the Jun-26 net cash; the scenario is a survivable but value-destroying path, not insolvency.
bear.tax_note: 48%: Mali extracts more (the 2023 Code's up-to-35% state share fully applied, higher royalty tiers) and Doropo's 10% free carry.

scenario_narratives.base: Gold glides from the ~$4,700 realised in H1-2026 to a $3,000 mid-cycle by 2030 while volumes roughly double: Syama recovers from the 2026 security/logistics disruptions as the sulphide conversion project (SSCP) reaches 4Mtpa, Doropo pours first gold in H1-2028 and ramps to ~200koz, and Mako's stockpiles run out around 2027-28 without a life extension. Owner FCF is roughly zero in 2026 and negative in 2027 (US$420m capex on a US$944m revenue year), then ~US$250m/yr from 2029. The valuation is therefore mostly Doropo-era cash flows discounted at 11%: terminal value is about half of EV, and the model implies an exit at 12x owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: Gold holds a $3,600-4,500 plateau (still below today's spot from 2028 on), central-bank demand keeps the floor, and execution goes to plan: Syama North lifts Syama to 250koz, Doropo delivers its 204koz first-five-year average on time and budget, the Mako life extension is approved, and the group reaches the 500koz run-rate in 2029. Margins hold ~50%, the Cote d'Ivoire fiscal take lowers the blended leakage to 40%, and the 14x cap reflects a diversified three-country producer rather than a Mali single-asset story.
scenario_narratives.bear: The Sahel stays hard and gold gives back its 2025-26 run: Syama's A21 pit and explosives supply keep disrupting output through 2027; Mali applies the 2023 Mining Code in full (state take up, ~48% combined leakage); gold reverts to $2,600 (the CY-2024 average, still above the $1,950 reserve price) from 2028; Mako ends with its stockpiles; Doropo slips to 2029 and overruns to ~US$650m. Two years of negative owner FCF eat most of the June-2026 net cash, and the business emerges as a ~380koz producer at 30% margins capped at 10x. A Barrick-style expropriation or asset seizure at Syama is NOT in this path; it would take the bear value materially lower and is the reason the bear weight is 30%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: single-region West African exposure with a recurring pattern of Mali disruption (2024 detention/settlement, 2025 Guinea permit revocations, the Sept-2026 guidance cut), a gold price at record levels that the base case already assumes retreats, and a US$516m greenfield build in the middle of the horizon. Bull at 25% because it needs three independent things to go right (gold plateau, Syama recovery, Doropo on time/budget), though the gold leg alone is currently true. Base 45%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Resolute is valued as an owner-FCF DCF on a mid-cycle gold price, not on spot. Three choices drive the number and are made explicit so they can be argued with. (1) Price: the base case deliberately walks realised gold from the US$4,712 achieved in H1-2026 down to US$3,000 by 2030 (the company's own Doropo DFS price), so the valuation does not rest on record gold persisting; the bull case is the plateau case and it too sits below today's spot from 2028. (2) Volume and capital: the value is mostly Doropo (first gold H1-2028) and a recovered Syama, which means 2026-27 owner FCF is near zero or negative while US$516m is spent; a 10-year horizon is used so the terminal year capitalises a ramped, steady-state producer rather than a construction year. (3) Jurisdiction: Mali risk is charged once, in the flows and weights (30% bear) plus a 1pp premium inside an 11% USD WACC applied identically to all scenarios; the 2024 Mali settlement (US$159.9m) is treated as sunk, and the lasting cost of the 2023 Mining Code is carried inside the Syama AISC and the 42-48% combined tax/NCI leakage. History matters less than usual: the reporting currency switched from AUD to USD in CY2019, and USD revenue growth since then is gold price rather than ounces (production fell 395koz to 277koz), so no historical CAGR is used as a forward driver. The balance sheet is anchored at 31-Dec-2025 with the Doropo deferred consideration (US$125m nominal) treated as debt and bullion excluded from cash because it was sold into H1-2026 revenue.
key_risks_to_valuation: Gold price: every US$100/oz on the mid-cycle assumption is roughly US$35-40m/yr of owner FCF at 450koz; the base already assumes a ~30% retreat from spot, so the risk is asymmetric to the upside on price alone but the bear ($2,600) is not remote.

Mali sovereign/security risk at Syama (~70% of near-term output): expropriation, further fiscal demands, or sustained explosives/logistics disruption; none of the three scenarios models loss of the asset.
Doropo execution: US$516m upfront capital, US$105m local bank financing not finalised at Sept-2026, first gold H1-2028; a one-year slip and 25% overrun are in the bear case only.
Mako mine life: stockpile processing ends ~2027; the base assumes no life extension, the bull assumes one.

Balance-sheet vintage: the H1-2026 interim (net cash US$317.4m at 30-Jun-26) is not yet extracted; the Dec-2025 anchor is used with H1-26 flows counted inside Y1. Re-anchor when the interim is extracted.
FX: intrinsic value is computed in USD and converted at 1.4249 USD/AUD; a 5% AUD move is ~A$0.05/share on the weighted IV.
